questions.question: A 62-year-old man presents with progressive intention tremor, gait ataxia, and executive dysfunction. Brain MRI shows symmetric hyperintensities in the middle cerebellar peduncles. His grandson was recently diagnosed with intellectual disability and macroorchidism. Molecular testing of the FMR1 gene in the grandfather is most likely to reveal which genetic mechanism?
options: RNA gain-of-function toxicity due to an FMR1 premutation (55–200 CGG repeats)
Complete transcriptional silencing of FMR1 due to promoter hypermethylation (>200 CGG repeats)
A haploinsufficiency frameshift mutation in exon 1 of FMR1
Microdeletion of chromosome 15q11.2-q13 including the FMR1 locus

questions.question: A child presents with neonatal hypotonia and global developmental delay. Genetic testing reveals maternal uniparental heterodisomy for chromosome 15, leading to Prader-Willi syndrome. Which meiotic or mitotic event is the primary cause of maternal uniparental heterodisomy?
options: Mitotic non-disjunction after fertilization
Post-zygotic duplication of a single maternal chromosome in a monosomic zygote
Maternal Meiosis I non-disjunction followed by trisomy rescue in the zygote
Maternal Meiosis II non-disjunction followed by trisomy rescue in the zygote

questions.question: A 34-year-old woman with mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) carries the m.3243A>G mutation. Her mother exhibits only mild sensorineural hearing loss, while her adult sister is completely asymptomatic despite carrying the same pathogenic variant. Which concept in mitochondrial genetics best accounts for this wide phenotypic variability?
options: Paternal leakage of normal mitochondrial genomes during fertilization
Genomic imprinting of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial factors
Somatic hypermutation during early blastocyst differentiation
Variable proportions of mutant and wild-type mtDNA copies across tissues (Heteroplasmy)

questions.question: A 2-day-old male infant presents with lethargy, poor feeding, hypothermia, and hyperventilation leading to respiratory alkalosis. Serum ammonia is markedly elevated (800 µmol/L). Quantitative amino acid analysis shows low plasma citrulline and high glutamine. Urine organic acid analysis shows significantly elevated orotic acid levels. Which enzyme deficiency is responsible for this metabolic condition?
options: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS1)
Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC)
Argininosuccinate synthetase (ASS1)
Phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH)

questions.question: A 4-year-old child presents with profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss present since birth and experiences recurrent syncopal episodes during physical exertion. An ECG demonstrates a corrected QT interval (QTc) of 530 ms. Genetic testing confirms homozygous loss-of-function mutations in KCNQ1. What is the diagnosis and its mode of inheritance?
options: Autosomal recessive; Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome
Autosomal dominant; Romano-Ward syndrome
X-linked recessive; Timothy syndrome
Autosomal dominant; Brugada syndrome
